products.name: The No-Cry Sleep Solution: Gentle Ways to Help Your Baby Sleep Through the Night

reviews.content: I had absolutely no idea just how valuable this book would become to me. It was recommended to me by my best friend who is now a midwife when my first child was 3 months old. I was just like SOOOO many mothers out there, literally OUT OF MY MIND with lack of sleep. I followed the book as best I could and by the time my daughter was 6-9 months old she was 100% sleeping through the night. The key message I would pass along to new mothers ""Don't expect overnight results"" and don't be afraid to be flexible. Pantley does a wonderful job of emphasizing the importance of flexibility. Sleeping is not a science, everyone (including babies) all do it differently. The important thing is that you learn about your baby and take your cues from him/her. I have recommended this book to every mother, new and experienced. I used the tips and tools in the book with my son who is now 2, and while it took twice as long to get him to STTN (18months old) it did work. I used the same methods / sleep plan (with some variation since I had 2 kids) and in the end it has worked. I now have 2 wonderful sleepers. Both children go to bed at a regular time everynight (8pm) and sleep a full 12 hours. If they wake up, they both put themselves back to sleep. Read it, follow it. . . it will change your life.
reviews.title: Completely Paid Off

reviews.content:
I purchased this book before I had my second child as my first child was a poor sleeper and I wanted to get it right with the second one from the beginning. I remember looking at children who could be put down to fall asleep on their own and thought to myself, that is impossible, why doesn't my child do this? Well now they do.
I began the simple and gentle techniques when my daughter was 6 weeks old and by 10 she was self settling with no crying, sucking her thumb to sleep. 2 weeks later she was sleeping through the night wihtout a murmer, 10-12 hours each night. It is bliss to know I can have a nights sleep without her waking up, especially considering her brother still wakes up in the night and comes into our bed. He is nearly 3 and his little sister could teach him a thing or 2 about how to sleep well! I have the second sleep book of Elizabeths that deals with toddlers and when I have the energy I will begin her techniques for him also. I know it will work, it is like a miracle and so simple and gentle to do!
One other thing to note she advocates breastfeeding throughout the book which I found excellent as I breastfeed and I think it will encourage others to do the same too. Brilliant book, recommend it to anyone
reviews.title: Excellent parenting book

reviews.content: This book has the tips and instruction to get your child to sleep and stay asleep while be loving and nurturing. This is a very loving wonderful approach like Attachment Parenting but more convenient for nowaday living. I started seriously following this program and saw amazing results within a week. This book will help your child get out of certain sleep associations (rocking to sleep, feeding to sleep) so they can fall asleep and stay asleep on their own. I recommend this book to anyone and everyone that has or ever will have children. This book will show you how to get your children on schedules so they are happier, healthier and have good sleep habits that will last their lifetime. I would never let my child (or any child or adult for that matter) cry themselves to sleep so I thank Elizabeth Pantley for writing this book.

reviews.content: I was never against letting my son cry it out. It bothered me some, but not to the extent of some. . . so I never thought I would need this book. But I found that the cry it out worked. . . but only for a while. Anytime something changed (vacation, teething, a late night out, time change, etc) I would have to do it all over again. Plus my son, who used to sleep 6-7 hours at a stretch started waking 8 times a night again. . . NOT GOOD! After two nights of applying the techniques in this book he was down to waking only 2 times (and one time was at 6:30. . . so pretty much morning although he usually slept another hour) I loved Pantley's approach of many techniques, instead of a one-size fits all. I worked most of the techniques into our routine and for a week now (including a camping trip) our son has stayed with only waking 1-2 times. I feel like a new woman!
reviews.title: Finally some sleep!

reviews.content: This book is truly great. I thought crying it out was the only solution. . . as soon as I started to read this book I was shaking my head in agreement with everything she was saying. I was so stressed about having my (beautiful/happy all the time except during sleep time) baby cry it out, until I found this life saving book. She is now sleeping one short nap in the morning, one longer nap in the afternoon and at least 6 hour stretches at a time during the night. I'm not going to lie to you and say it happened overnight but we followed the suggestions and it worked. No crying it out for our family! If you are like me and everyone (doctors, friends and family) is telling you CIO is the only way just buy this book and you'll see it isn't and there really is a better way!

reviews.content:
As a first time mother, I cannot tell you how many people try to give me advice on how to raise my baby. My son had no trouble sleeping through the night, right from the second month. Things were going so well, that we moved him to his own room at 2 1/2 months, where he would sleep 8 and 9 hour stretches. Then, he went through a growth spurt and was up every 2 hours! We had no idea what to do (since we were so spoiled from the beginning). Since I am going back to work soon, I knew I needed to try to solve this problem! SO many other parents tried to tell me to let him ""cry it out"". I thought, ""really? A 4 month old? That seems too young!"" We tried it one night and it was awful. It broke my heart, and it just didn't feel right. We are first time parents and I was so afraid of not doing the right thing. Every night, as it got closer to bedtime, I would have more and more anxiety, Finally, my husband said, ""screw it, he's sleeping with us! I love him and I want him with us. "" Shortly after, I purchased this book and we are now in the process of working on our sleep plan. Things have already improved. 

I especially like Elizabeth's suggestion about the lovey toy. I chose 2 soft loveys for my son and let him hold and snuggle it while he nursed and when he napped. One night, when he was trying to settle in his cradle, I stroked his face with the lovey. He took my lead and started doing it by himself to calm himself down. I even went a step further and put the lovey in the dryer for a few minutes so it was warm for him. Last night, he put himself to sleep in his cradle without so much as a whimper! Not only that, he slept 8 hours straight! 

Another thing I like about this book is that it gives MANY ideas for parents to try. I did not try everything the book suggested, I just chose things I thought might be right for my son. Pantley stresses the importance of being consistent with your sleep plan, so make sure you choose things that you are able to do, night after night. 

In conclusion, I have already lent this book to a good friend of mine with a 9 month old! Buy the book, it's an easy read and you will get something out of it! There are ways to get your baby to sleep without crying, trust me!!!!!
reviews.title: Tired of people telling me to let my baby ""cry it out""

reviews.content:
My eight-month-old son was still waking up to eat every night, and I was hoping to find a way to help him sleep through the night without using the dreadful ""cry-it-out"" approach. I have Dr. Sears' ""The Baby Book"" and ""Secrets of the Baby Whisperer"" by Tracy Hogg, both of whom I appreciate for their gentle and child-centered parenting philosophies. But I wanted something that was focused just on sleep. I have also read ""Healthy Sleep Habits, Happy Child"" by Marc Weissbluth and ""Becoming Baby Wise"" by Gary Ezzo, and was left feeling guilty for not wanting my child to cry himself to sleep. I was sick of feeling like a bad mother because I wanted something more loving for my son. 

This book was exactly what I was looking for! It was tender and sympathetic to both babies and tired mothers. The book not only provided lots of great solutions to improve your baby's sleep, but also had the compassion of an actual mother who has gone through these same problems herself. I found her advice very helpful, and within three weeks my baby was sleeping through the night without a single crying episode! The book also addresses naps and the importance of establishing a routine (not a schedule) to help your baby's body ease more easily into sleep. I am so glad I found this book, and would highly recommend it to anyone who wants their baby to have a good night's rest without the tears!
reviews.title: Everything I hoped for!
